name: Ordine
classification_notes: Modern geometric sans-serif built around perfectly circular counters in letters like o, e and a. Avoids the sterility typical of strict geometric designs through a two-story g and a softened horizontal bar on the e for legibility. Distributed as a variable font spanning Thin to Black with true italics at each weight. Oblique variants also available alongside the italics per the foundry page.
summary: A geometric sans-serif variable font with perfectly circular counters, nine weights with true italics, and broad multilingual coverage across 200-plus languages.
description: Ordine is built around circular counters in its key letterforms, giving it a clean geometric foundation softened by a two-story g and a subtly modified e that improve on-screen legibility. The family spans Thin to Black as a variable font with a full set of true italics, making it flexible across editorial and branding contexts. Lighter weights suit running text and editorial work; heavier cuts lean toward sportswear, packaging and identity design.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza Type describes Ordine as a modern geometric sans designed for digital-first work, with its circular geometry, balanced proportions and responsive variable font axis intended to suit contexts from fashion branding to cultural editorial. The foundry highlights its 200-plus language support and oblique variants as suited to international and multi-platform projects.

name: Piccola
classification_notes: A single-weight calligraphic script with bouncy, fluid letterforms inspired by pen-and-paper lettering. No italic (the script itself serves that role), no condensed variants, no width range. OpenType stylistic sets provide alternate forms for select characters. Latin Extended coverage.
summary: A calligraphic script with soft, bouncy letterforms and a single Regular weight, suited to food, lifestyle and artisan branding.
description: Piccola is a handcrafted script by Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González, drawing on calligraphic tradition to produce fluid, pen-drawn letterforms with generous curves and a bouncy rhythm. A single Regular weight ships with stylistic alternates, ligatures and initial forms across a 367-character Latin Extended set. It reads warmly at display sizes and fits branding, packaging, café signage and greeting cards where a personal, handmade quality is the brief.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describes Piccola as born from the art of calligraphy, with soft curves and fluid connections that replicate the natural rhythm of pen on paper. The foundry positions it for branding, packaging, editorial and any project requiring a personal, human touch, from display headlines down to intimate text settings.

name: Performa
classification_notes: Grotesque-geometric hybrid sans-serif; six widths (Compressed to Wide), nine weights (Thin to Black), all with matching italics; 108 static fonts plus a variable font with 252 named instances across weight and width axes.
summary: A grotesque-geometric hybrid sans-serif superfamily spanning six widths and nine weights, each with matching italics, plus a variable font covering both axes.
description: Performa blends grotesque and geometric design sensibilities into a single coherent family, released by Resistenza's Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González in 2024. Six widths (Compressed to Wide) and nine weights (Thin to Black) each carry a matching italic, giving 108 static fonts in total. A variable font adds continuous interpolation across both axes with 252 named instances, and the family covers 200+ Latin-script languages.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza positions Performa as a versatile family for branding, editorial work and digital interfaces, marrying the structure of geometric type with the texture of grotesque design across an unusually wide range of widths and weights.

name: Onni
classification_notes: Contemporary geometric sans-serif with deliberate eccentricities: characters sit at slightly varying angles along an inconsistent baseline (described as "kinetic alignment"), lowercase "e" has a triangular cutout aperture, and the "R" tail curves beyond conventional geometric construction. Upright only; no italic. 10 weights plus variable font axis. Display-leaning despite the broad weight range.
summary: A ten-weight geometric sans-serif from Resistenza with Swiss modernist bones and deliberate imperfections – unsteady baseline, angled characters, a triangular aperture on the "e" – aimed squarely at display and branding work.
description: Onni is a geometric sans-serif by Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González, debuted by Resistenza in early 2026. It builds on a grid of perfect circles and rectangles but then subverts it: characters tilt slightly along an inconsistent baseline, the lowercase "e" carries a triangular cutout, and the "R" sweeps past conventional geometry. Ten weights from Hairline to Black, with a variable font option, make it versatile in scale, though the quirky detailing keeps it best suited to headlines, packaging and identity work rather than running text.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza positions Onni as precision balanced with playful disruption – a typeface that explores the territory between Swiss modernism and experimental typography. They recommend it for youth-oriented branding, tech startups, creative studio identities, editorial design and packaging, framing it as a display choice where personality matters more than traditional legibility.

name: Nautica
classification_notes: High-contrast pointed-nib script inspired by Copperplate's ductus. Decorative caps; ligatures and swashes drawn from brush pen aesthetics. The slant is intrinsic to the script design — there is no separate italic.
summary: A high-contrast Copperplate-inspired script by Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González, spanning three weights with over 1,000 glyphs and extensive OpenType decoration.
description: Nautica draws on the Copperplate ductus to produce a narrow, pointed-nib script with strong contrast and assertive personality. It ships in Regular, Medium and Bold, plus a supplementary Icons and Knots set, and packs in ligatures, swashes and contextual alternates across more than 1,000 glyphs. Language support extends to 200+ scripts, though its use cases are firmly in formal branding, packaging and editorial contexts that call for calligraphic flair.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describes Nautica as a script typeface based on Copperplate's ductus — high in contrast, with a strong character and a comprehensive set of professional typographic features. The foundry notes that ligatures and swashes take inspiration from brush pen aesthetics, and the family includes a decorative icons and knots collection to complement the lettering.

name: Modern Love
classification_notes: Hand-painted brush script drawn with a pointed brush and walnut ink, prioritising casual lettering over formal calligraphy. High contrast with flowing letterforms. Spans four distinct stylistic variants: a clean upright, a washed-out Grunge version, a rough-edged Rough version, and a handwritten caps companion (Caps) drawn with a pointed nib and Indian ink. Each sub-family ships with a Slanted companion. OpenType alternates, swashes, and ornaments are included.
summary: A hand-painted brush script family in four stylistic variants – clean, grunge, rough and caps – drawn with a pointed brush and walnut ink by Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González.
description: Modern Love is a brush script family from Resistenza Type, designed by Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González using a pointed brush and walnut ink to capture casual lettering rather than formal calligraphy. The family spans four variants – Modern Love (clean), Grunge (washed-out, vintage), Rough (crunchy rough edges) and Caps (a handwritten sans drawn with a pointed nib and Indian ink) – each available with a slanted companion. OpenType alternates, swashes and ornaments extend the expressive range for headline and packaging work.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza is an italo-spanish type foundry co-founded by Giuseppe Salerno in Torino and Paco González in Valencia, specialising in brush scripts and calligraphic typefaces developed through traditional pen-and-paper methods before digitisation.

name: Kiosq
classification_notes: Single-style display typeface inspired by hand-painted signage and tiki culture. Bold three-dimensional letterforms with drop shadows and energetic baseline variations. Calligraphic brush stroke influences with organic irregularities give it a hand-lettered character. Slightly condensed proportions are part of the design, not a separate variant.
summary: A single-style hand-painted display face drawing on tiki culture and mid-century sign painting, with bold three-dimensional letterforms and energetic baseline variation.
description: Kiosq arrives with drop shadows, bouncy baselines and calligraphic brush strokes that evoke sun-bleached vintage signage. Its slightly condensed proportions suit headlines and packaging where a retro-tropical mood is the point. At a single style with no italic or weight range, its application is intentionally narrow.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describes Kiosq as capturing the spirited essence of hand-painted signage with a tropical twist, born from tiki culture and mid-century sign painting traditions – combining fluid brush strokes with confident calligraphic flair for headlines, branding and packaging that call for tropical warmth and vintage charm.

name: Sidera
classification_notes: High-contrast serif with wedge serifs and flared terminals, drawing on transitional and calligraphic traditions. Slanted variants are labelled "Slanted" rather than "Italic" – likely mechanical obliques rather than redrawn italic letterforms.
summary: A high-contrast editorial serif from Italian studio Resistenza, spanning nine weights with slanted companions and a variable axis, aimed at magazine layouts, luxury packaging and typographic identities.
description: Sidera draws on transitional serif and calligraphic traditions, combining sharp wedge serifs with flared terminals and strong stroke contrast. Nine weights run from Thin to Black, each with a slanted counterpart, and a variable font covers the full range in a single file. Oldstyle figures and ornamental flourishes broaden its reach across upmarket editorial and identity work.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describes Sidera as a refined, high-contrast serif with a strong editorial voice, built for magazines, cultural publications, luxury packaging and typographic identities, with support for 150 or more languages.

name: Effimera
classification_notes: High-contrast modern serif in the Didone tradition. Strong vertical stress, dramatic thick-to-thin stroke contrast, crisp hairline serifs, and distinctive ball terminals on 'g' and 'a'. Draws on Bodoni and Didot. Offered in display and text optical cuts, with a width axis spanning UltraCondensed to UltraExpanded. No italic. Single weight throughout.
summary: A high-contrast Didone serif with nine widths, matching Text cuts, and a variable font — built for luxury branding and fashion editorial where drama and elegance are the brief.
description: Effimera is a Didone-classification display serif defined by dramatic stroke contrast, crisp hairline serifs, and distinctive ball terminals on 'g' and 'a'. The family spans nine widths — UltraCondensed to UltraExpanded — each available in both display and text optical sizes, with a variable font adding a width axis for granular control. Without an italic or weight axis it is a one-register instrument, but within that register it covers an unusually broad set of proportions for the category.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza Type is an independent Italian-Spanish digital foundry run by calligrapher-designer Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González, producing commercial display, text, and decorative typefaces sold direct and through major distributors.

name: LeKick
classification_notes: Fraktur-inspired display blackletter drawn with flat brush and ink. Two-style family: a clean Regular and a Brush variant that exposes the underlying stroke logic of each letterform. No weight range – the distinction is stylistic rather than optical.
summary: A Fraktur-inspired display blackletter from Resistenza, offered in Regular and Brush styles, built with flat-brush ink technique and winner of a 2023 Communication Arts Award of Excellence for Typography.
description: LeKick draws from the Fraktur tradition with a contemporary sensibility, constructed using flat brush and ink for use in headlines, book covers, packaging and branding. It comes in two stylistic variants: a standard Regular and a Brush version that makes the underlying stroke logic of each letterform visible. It won a Communication Arts Award of Excellence for Typography in 2023 – a meaningful credential for a display face with this kind of niche brief.
foundry_blurb: Designed with a flat brush and ink, LeKick is a blackletter display face drawing on Fraktur with a modern edge. Available in Regular and Brush styles, it is suited to headlines, book covers, posters, labels and branding work.

name: Oddity Script
classification_notes: Single-weight calligraphic script with deliberately inverted stroke contrast – thin where you'd expect thick, thick where you'd expect thin. Inspired by the skeletal structure of Nautica with contrast reversed. Selective exceptions in certain letterforms preserve rhythm and legibility. Heavy 1970s period character.
summary: A single-weight calligraphic script with inverted stroke contrast and a strong 1970s nostalgia character, suited to display use in posters, branding and packaging.
description: Oddity Script takes the skeleton of English calligraphy and flips its contrast: strokes that would conventionally be thick are drawn thin, and vice versa. The effect is distinctive but narrow in application, best at large sizes where its 70s period personality can read clearly. OpenType features add swash capitals and alternate glyphs, giving some flexibility within the single weight.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describes Oddity Script as a calligraphic font with reversed contrast, with selective exceptions in certain letters to maintain legibility and rhythm. The design is rooted in English calligraphy and takes the Nautica skeleton as its structural starting point before inverting the contrast entirely. The foundry frames it as lo-fi nostalgia – a tribute to a past era with a contemporary finish.

name: Squadra Stencil
classification_notes: Geometric stencil display typeface with a rectilinear, modular structure. 18 styles across 9 weights with full italic complement. Contemporary stencil treatment drawing from industrial signage and sci-fi aesthetics rather than traditional military stencil conventions. No width variants.
summary: A geometric stencil typeface spanning nine weights with matching italics, built from the angular vocabulary of Resistenza's Squadra family with precisely placed letterform cuts for a contemporary industrial character.
description: Designed by Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González, Squadra Stencil takes the rectilinear structure of Squadra and introduces carefully positioned letterform breaks to achieve the stencil effect without sacrificing legibility. The cuts draw from industrial signage and sci-fi aesthetics rather than standard military stencil conventions, giving the typeface a high-tech, graphic edge. With 18 styles across nine weights, it suits bold poster work, editorial headers and branding for technology or industrial-themed projects.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describe Squadra Stencil as "squarish, strong and solid", a stencil companion to their Squadra family combining elements of industrial signage, brutalist typography and futuristic aesthetics. The rectilinear structure and strategically placed breaks maintain legibility while delivering a graphic, high-tech impact across a wide weight range.

name: Qimbo
classification_notes: Positioned by Resistenza in their logos/identity category alongside geometric and humanist sans families (Squadra, Onni, Norman). The foundry article describes it as having "restrained energy" suitable for wordmarks — suggesting a structured, contemporary display face rather than a novelty or script. The product page could not be rendered directly (JavaScript-gated), so weights and precise style details could not be confirmed beyond a single Regular style. The "stencil/handmade" description returned by some automated fetches appears to be AI-hallucinated and is contradicted by the foundry's own editorial copy, which emphasises restraint and professional applicability.
summary: A restrained, contemporary display typeface from Resistenza Type, built for identity work where presence matters but experiment does not.
description: Qimbo is one of Resistenza's newer releases, positioned squarely in the foundry's logos category alongside geometric and humanist sans families. The foundry describes it as having the kind of restrained energy that makes it immediately usable in identity work – strong enough to anchor a wordmark, refined enough not to overpower it. It suits brands that want to feel current without veering into the experimental.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describes Qimbo as a strong contender for brands wanting a fresh, contemporary feel without sacrificing refinement, positioned for wordmarks and identity applications where typographic confidence is the priority.

name: Revolute
classification_notes: Geometric stencil sans-serif display typeface. Six weight levels (Light, Regular, Medium, Bold, Black, Display) each offered in upright and slanted forms, totalling 12 static styles. Also published as a variable font with weight and slant axes. Designed as a contemporary revival of H. Brünnel's Resolut, released by Fonderie Nebiolo, Turin, 1937. Slanted variants are mechanically sloped, not true italics.
summary: A geometric stencil revival of H. Brünnel's 1937 Resolut from Fonderie Nebiolo, offered across six weights with slanted companions and a variable font version.
description: Revolute takes its cue from the Resolut typeface designed by H. Brünnel for Fonderie Nebiolo in Turin in 1937. Designed by Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González and released in 2024, it carries clean geometric letterforms with the characteristic optical cuts of stencil construction across six weights, each paired with a slanted companion. Practical enough for branding, signage and headlines, though the stencil form keeps it firmly in display-only territory.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza positions Revolute as a stencil typeface inspired by the 1937 Resolut from Fonderie Nebiolo, combining historical letterform references with contemporary construction to produce balanced, harmonious type suited to branding, signage and display work.

name: Monologo
classification_notes: Fixed-width family with an unconventional glyph skeleton built for screen clarity. Unusually broad for a monospaced design: four stylistic subfamilies (standard with Italic, Script, Rounded, Fax) across three weights, plus variable font support. Latin, Greek and Cyrillic scripts included.
summary: A contemporary fixed-width family with an unconventional glyph skeleton and unusually broad stylistic range for a monospace, spanning standard, script, rounded and fax subfamilies across three weights with Latin, Greek and Cyrillic coverage.
description: Monologo is engineered for legibility on screen and at small sizes, with consistent spacing and a distinctive skeleton that lifts it above utilitarian workhorse monospaces. Four subfamilies – Italic, Script, Rounded and Fax – give it a broader palette than most fixed-width designs: the Fax cut adds a deliberately grungy, distressed aesthetic while Script softens the mechanical rigidity of the form. All 14 styles support Latin, Greek and Cyrillic across 200+ languages, and variable font versions are available in OTF, TTF and WOFF2.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza pitches Monologo as a font for those who speak in code and poetry – a fixed-width family built for digital legibility, with an unconventional glyph skeleton that gives it more personality than the utilitarian monospaces it competes with.

name: Crispo Script
classification_notes: Formal pointed-nib calligraphy script. Single weight. Inherently slanted cursive letterforms with ligatures, swash characters and alternates via OpenType. Not designed for body text; squarely in decorative/display territory.
summary: A single-weight pointed-pen calligraphy script by Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González, built around flowing ligatures and swash alternates for wedding, branding and logotype work.
description: Crispo is a pointed-pen calligraphy script released by Resistenza in 2023, drawn to capture the fluid strokes and precision of traditional nib work. It ships as a single Regular weight with OpenType ligatures, swashes and alternates that reward careful setting. The result is an elegant but narrow-use face suited to wedding stationery, luxury packaging and logotypes rather than running text.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describes Crispo as crafted through the delicate strokes of pointed pen calligraphy, with each character, ligature and swash designed to show the artistry and timeless grace of the craft.

name: Furbo
classification_notes: Monospaced variable typeface with three axes: Width (Condensed to Expanded), Contrast (Low to High), and Turbo (a distortion/expression axis that introduces fluid, energetic deformation). The mono grid persists across the width range but the Turbo axis pushes it firmly into display territory. 30 static styles plus one variable font, structured as 5 widths × 3 contrast levels × 2 (standard/Turbo).
summary: A variable monospaced display typeface with width, contrast and Turbo axes that span tight geometric mono through wildly distorted high-contrast forms.
description: Furbo is a monospaced variable typeface built for display and motion work, offering 30 static styles across five widths and three contrast levels. Its third axis, Turbo, introduces deliberate distortion that pushes letterforms into kinetic, energetic territory beyond anything a conventional mono family offers. It suits editorial headlines, title sequences and expressive graphic work, rather than text setting or UI use.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describe Furbo as designed for bold expression, with letterforms that shift between rigid geometry and fluid distortion. Three variable axes – Width, Contrast and Turbo – let designers move from clean monospaced type to kinetic, pulsing compositions, positioning the family as a tool for those who want something unpredictable and dynamic.

name: Pressato
classification_notes: Uppercase-only reverse-contrast display sans. Thick where conventional type is thin, thin where it is thick. Sharp corners, rectangular counters and a geometry that references early tech and sci-fi typography. Three variable axes: weight, width and slant. The slant axis produces deliberately skewed, angular effects rather than a conventional italic.
summary: A variable reverse-contrast display family, commissioned by a Turin coffee bookshop, with three axes covering weight, width and slant across 12 static cuts.
description: Pressato is an uppercase-only display family from Resistenza Type, designed in collaboration with Pressato Coffee Bookshop in Turin. It applies reverse-contrast logic with sharp corners and rectangular counters, drawing on early sci-fi and tech aesthetics. Three variable axes – weight, width and slant – yield 12 static fonts plus a variable version, making it a usable choice for distinctive branding and editorial headlines.
foundry_blurb: Built as a direct collaboration with Pressato Coffee Bookshop in Turin, the typeface channels the shop's contemporary artistic identity through reverse-contrast construction and a slant axis that produces deliberately angular, geometric effects suited to branding and display work.

name: Squadra
classification_notes: Squared geometric sans-serif drawing directly from Eurostile's mid-century modernist lineage. Consistent squared terminals, low stroke contrast, uniform letterform construction, and a strong technical character. Sits comfortably in the geometric sans tradition alongside faces like Eurostile and Titillium.
summary: A squared geometric sans-serif spanning nine weights with matching italics, drawing on Eurostile's mid-century modernist blueprint and adapting it for contemporary branding and editorial work.
description: Squadra takes its cues from Eurostile – the squared-terminal sans designed by Aldo Novarese and Alessandro Butti – reinterpreting that geometric rigour for present-day typographic demands. Designers Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González extend the family across nine weights from Thin to Black, each paired with a matching italic, giving it the range for sustained editorial and identity work. A variable font ships alongside the 18 static styles, spanning both roman and italic axes.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describe Squadra as a squarish, strong and solid contemporary sans-serif family inspired by Eurostile. They position it as a reinterpretation of that typeface's geometric elegance and modernist character, refined for current needs and suited equally to display and text settings across branding, editorial layouts, web interfaces and signage.

name: Norman
classification_notes: Condensed proportions with extreme stroke contrast built on an expansion-based construction; distinctive oblique stress axis gives it a contemporary, fashion-inflected character. Related to the Didone tradition but interpreted through a modern display lens rather than a revival framework.
summary: A condensed, high-contrast display serif with an oblique axis, designed for editorial headlines and fashion-forward branding.
description: Norman is built on an expansion-based construction – condensed proportions with sharp stroke contrast and a deliberate oblique stress that gives it a contemporary edge. Designed by Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González and released by Resistenza in 2020, it ships in five weights with matching italics, a variable version and a stencil extension. It has appeared on Emily Ratajkowski's book cover, Guitar World magazine and various high-profile music releases – credible real-world deployment for a display-only face.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describe Norman as a contemporary condensed serif based on expansion, with an oblique axis added to give it a modern, self-confident feel. They recommend it for big titles, magazine layouts and editorial display work.

name: Liquida
classification_notes: Decorative brush script with pronounced slanted inclination. All characters drawn by hand with brush and walnut ink on paper, with deliberate ink drops creating a trickling effect throughout the letterforms. Single style; OpenType alternates, ligatures and swashes provide some variation within that single weight.
summary: A single-weight brush script drawn with real walnut ink, where deliberate ink-drop trickling effects give every letterform a genuinely fluid, liquified quality.
description: Liquida is a decorative script by Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González, with every character drawn by hand using brush and walnut ink to produce a distinctive trickling effect. The slanted letterforms are supported by alternates, ligatures and swashes via OpenType, offering some variety within a narrow display register. It suits logotypes, packaging and short-form headline work where the ink-soaked aesthetic is the entire point.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza bills Liquida as their most fluid typeface, drawn entirely in walnut ink on paper to capture real ink drops trickling down letterforms, making each character feel genuinely handcrafted.

name: Gotti
classification_notes: Geometric sans-serif drawing on Bauhaus grid structure with 1970s-inflected detailing. Upright-only; no italics confirmed across MyFonts listing of 9 styles. Variable font also available covering the full weight axis.
summary: A nine-weight geometric sans-serif designed in Göteborg, Gotti blends Bauhaus grid principles with 1970s warmth for display and branding use.
description: Designed by Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González and released in November 2023, Gotti takes a rigid Bauhaus skeleton and tempers it with rounded, decade-specific details borrowed from the seventies. Nine weights from Thin to Black – plus a variable font – give it sufficient range for headlines, logotypes and packaging. It works best at large sizes where the geometry and retro character can read clearly; at text sizes the personality is lost.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describes Gotti as a flexible family of ten fonts that fuses Bauhaus essence with the spirited vibes of the seventies, built on geometric simplicity and razor-sharp lines, and intended for display use, advertising and branding.

name: TotalBlack
classification_notes: A clean, neutral grotesque in the classic European grotesk tradition. Nine weights from Thin to Heavy plus a dedicated Display variant, all with matching italics. Also released as a variable font. No condensed or extended widths. The Display style functions as an optical variant for large-scale use rather than a pure weight step.
summary: A neutral nine-weight grotesque from Resistenza with italics throughout, a dedicated Display cut for large-scale work and a variable font release.
description: TotalBlack is a clean grotesque sans-serif in nine weights – Thin to Heavy – each with a matching italic, plus a Display variant built for large-scale use. Designed by Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González at Resistenza, it draws on the classic grotesque tradition and ships as a variable font with OpenType alternates and coverage for 300+ languages. Suited to brand, editorial and UI work that calls for a serious, unfussy tone.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describe TotalBlack as a modern font family inspired by classic grotesque typefaces, built for logos, magazines and graphic design. Nine weights with italics, standard and contextual alternates, a formidable Display variant and language coverage spanning 300+ scripts.

name: Lettera
classification_notes: Connected monoline script with rounded nib construction, evoking mid-20th-century penmanship. Three weights vary stroke thickness while preserving the monoline character. Includes alternates, swashes and ending forms intended for headline and wordmark use.
summary: A connected monoline script in three weights, drawing on mid-century penmanship and rounded-nib handwriting for decorative headline use.
description: Lettera is a connected monoline script by Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González that channels mid-20th-century handwriting through a rounded nib construction. Three styles – Script, Script Medium and Script Thick – span a range of stroke weight while maintaining the romantic, naive character. Around 400 glyphs include alternates, swashes and ending forms, making it best suited to decorative headlines and wordmarks.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describe Lettera as delivering 20th-century penmanship vibes via a rounded nib, carrying the soul of a romantic naive hand. Connected letterforms with some 400 glyphs – including alternates, swashes and ending forms – aimed at decorative custom headlines and wordmarks.

name: Auster Slab
classification_notes: Slab serif with inverted (antique/Italian) stress – horizontal strokes are thicker than verticals, opposite to conventional serif construction. Forms were developed by hand with a flat brush before pencil refinement and digitisation. Companion to the Auster reversed-contrast sans, the slab version shares the same stroke logic but adds squared serifs that reinforce its period character. Ten upright weights from Thin to Heavy, each with a matching italic, giving the family genuine typographic range.
summary: A reversed-contrast slab companion to Resistenza's Auster sans, spanning ten weights with matching italics and a hand-drawn character suited to editorial, branding and display work.
description: Auster Slab carries the inverted stroke stress of Resistenza's Auster sans into a slab serif form, where thick horizontals against thinner verticals give the family a distinctive character without tipping into novelty. The ten-weight range from Thin to Heavy – each paired with a matching italic, 20 styles total – gives it genuine breadth across display and text settings. Designed by Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González, the letterforms were first laid down with a flat brush, refined in pencil on tracing paper, then carefully digitised with full OpenType feature support.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza is an independent digital type foundry and font shop run by Italian designer Giuseppe Salerno and Spanish designer Paco González, offering professional desktop, web and app licences alongside custom type design, branding and lettering services.

name: Flipante
classification_notes: Geometric display sans-serif built on a pronounced width axis, running from ultra condensed to expanded. The construction uses tubular letterforms with decorative ink traps and rounded curves rather than a neutral grotesque skeleton. No true italic – each of the five widths is paired with an oblique (slanted) companion only. Also released as a variable font on the width axis.
summary: A geometric display sans spanning ultra condensed to expanded across five widths, defined by tubular letterforms, prominent ink traps and rounded curves, with oblique companions and a variable font option.
description: Flipante, designed by Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González for Resistenza Type, is a display sans-serif whose tubular construction, decorative ink traps and expressive curves give it a personality well beyond a neutral grotesque. The family covers five widths from ultra condensed to expanded, each paired with a slanted companion, and the entire range is also available as a variable font on the width axis. It is aimed squarely at branding, packaging and headline work in print and digital contexts.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describe Flipante as both aesthetic and functional, with tubular shapes, ink traps and juicy curves that make it adaptable for branding and packaging work across print and digital. The condensed-to-extended range is positioned as its core strength, allowing it to flex to fit almost any project's spatial requirements.

name: Red Oak
classification_notes: Wedge (or Latin) serif with narrow, tapered serifs characteristic of the style. Upright-only family spanning four widths and six weights, giving it a broad range from compressed headlines to wider text settings. The contrast is moderate, balancing legibility with a faintly vintage, engraved quality.
summary: A 24-style wedge-serif family from Resistenza spanning four widths and six weights, with narrow tapered serifs that give it a faintly vintage, engraved character suited to editorial and branding work.
description: Red Oak is a wedge-serif with narrow, elegantly tapered serifs that sit somewhere between classical Latin letterforms and contemporary display type. Its four width variants – Condensed, Regular, Wide and Expanded – each run across six weights from Thin to Black, giving designers genuine range across both setting size and spatial needs. There are no italic cuts, so it works best in contexts where weight and width alone carry the typographic hierarchy.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza positions Red Oak as a fresh take on the wedge-serif tradition – narrow serifs that reach out with finesse, balancing vintage engraving references against clean, contemporary proportions. The foundry highlights its flexibility across branding, magazine layouts and digital use.

name: Turquoise
classification_notes: Brush-drawn Roman capitals with calligraphic terminal serifs; single-weight display face derived from Capitalis Romana study and foundational calligraphy practised at the Tipobrda workshop in Slovenia. Companion pieces — Turquoise Sans, Turquoise Inline and Turquoise Tuscan — are separate typeface families on the Resistenza site. No lowercase in the original Turquoise; small caps included.
summary: A single-weight brush-drawn Roman capitals display face with calligraphic terminal serifs, swashes and ornaments suited to luxury headline and packaging work.
description: Turquoise draws on Capitalis Romana practice and foundational calligraphy, each letter formed with a broad-edged brush to produce characteristic unfinished terminal serifs. It ships with small caps, discretionary ligatures, swashes and nature-inspired ornaments via OpenType, making it well suited to headlines, luxury packaging and visual identities. In use it has appeared on Hanbury Gin, olive oil branding and theatrical advertising.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describe Turquoise as Roman Capitals designed smoothly by brush rather than carved in stone, with terminal serifs derived from fundamental stroke studies practised at the Tipobrda calligraphy workshop in Slovenia. They position it for headlines and body text in advertising, packaging and visual identities, where its delicate curves and endings give work a harmonious, distinctive character.

name: Big Mamma
classification_notes: Informal handdrawn slab serif with deliberately uneven strokes and visible hand-construction irregularities. Casual, organic character — closer to display lettering than a workhorse slab. Not a revival of any historical model; the irregularity is the design intent.
summary: A handdrawn slab with deliberately rough, organic letterforms suited to artisanal food, children's and organic-branding contexts.
description: Big Mamma is a handdrawn slab serif from Resistenza Type, released in 2020 by designers Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González. Its uneven strokes and DIY roughness give it a handmade character well suited to food packaging, children's materials and organic branding. The family is compact at three styles — Regular, Italic and Back Slanted — which limits its versatility beyond those specific display uses.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describe Big Mamma as a handrawn slab for flexible purposes, combining a DIY effect and handmade touch intended to bring an artisanal quality to design layouts.

name: Lafleur
classification_notes: Ornamental display face with strong Liberty/Art Nouveau character. Two width variants only (Regular and Wide); no weight spectrum. Letterforms reference curvilinear, foliate detailing from late 19th-century Italian Stile Liberty architecture. No italic cut.
summary: An ornamental Art Nouveau display face inspired by the Fenoglio-Lafleur Liberty building in Turin, available in Regular and Wide widths.
description: Lafleur translates the foliate, curvilinear detailing of Turin's late 19th-century Stile Liberty architecture into type. Designed by Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González and released in 2023, the family spans just two widths with no weight range. It works at headline scale for book covers, fashion packaging and editorial contexts where period ornamentation is the point.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describe Lafleur as a decorative face with a remarkable Art Nouveau flair from the 19th century, drawn from the iconic Fenoglio-Lafleur Liberty building in Turin. They position it for book covers, packaging, branding, editorial, web, advertising and apparel, describing its potential purposes as endless.

name: Superpop
classification_notes: Rounded geometric sans-serif with brushy, script-influenced letterforms. The geometric structure is softened by calligraphic instincts in the stroke details, placing it between a conventional sans and a script face. Designed strictly for display use – not suitable for body text or editorial work.
summary: A rounded geometric display sans with brushy, script-influenced letterforms, offered in five weights with matching italics and an outline variant, plus a variable font.
description: Superpop blends geometric construction with calligraphic instincts – each letterform carries a softness that sits somewhere between a conventional sans and a script face. Designed by Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González at Resistenza, it comes in five weights plus an outline cut, each with a matching italic, alongside a variable font for smooth weight interpolation. Its sweet, fizzy character suits food and drink branding, children's publishing and social media content where warmth and energy matter.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describe Superpop as "sweet and gentle, a rounded geometric sans with a brushy script twist" – a display family where geometric letterforms carry calligraphic instincts. Available across five weights and an outline, each with a matching italic, plus a variable font version for smooth interpolation.

name: Turquoise Sans
classification_notes: Humanist sans-serif with subtle terminal swellings derived from classical Roman capitals, bridging the gap between geometric construction and calligraphic warmth. The Inline style applies a decorative hollow treatment to the Regular, making it purely a display variant. Only two styles exist in the family — no weight range, no italics — which limits its utility as a workhorse.
summary: A humanist sans-serif with subtly swelled terminals referencing classical Roman capitals, offered in two styles – Regular and a decorative Inline – by the designers of the original Turquoise script.
description: Turquoise Sans translates the calligraphic character of Resistenza's bestselling Turquoise script into a clean sans-serif form, with terminal swellings that nod to the pen-drawn origins of Roman letterforms. The two-style family covers a functional Regular and a decorative Inline variant suited to headlines and brand work. With no weights beyond Regular and no italic, it works best as a display or identity typeface for cultural institutions, publishers and brand projects that want historical resonance alongside contemporary form.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describes Turquoise Sans as technically a sans-serif that carries subtle swellings at the terminal strokes – an homage to classical Roman capital letterforms and to the brushy tradition of their bestselling Turquoise script. The foundry recommends it for cultural institutions, publishing and brand identities that value historical reference alongside contemporary design.

name: Afrobeat Nova
classification_notes: Single-weight inline/multilinear display face. Each letterform is built from parallel strokes giving an optical, retro-striped effect. Geometric construction with strong 1970s psychedelic influences. A 2024 redesign of Resistenza's 2010 Afrobeat; uppercase was reworked and lowercase fully rebuilt. No italic, no condensed, no weight range.
summary: A single-weight multilinear display face that reimagines Resistenza's 2010 Afrobeat with a new uppercase and a fully reworked lowercase, channelling 1970s psychedelic poster aesthetics.
description: Afrobeat Nova updates the 2010 original with a revised uppercase set and a completely rebuilt lowercase, both constructed around the family's signature multilinear strokes that give every letterform a retro, optically-striped quality. The design draws on the visual culture of Afrobeat music – the funk and psychedelia of 1960s and 70s Nigeria – translated into geometric type. A single-weight display face, it works at large sizes on posters, event flyers, album covers and advertising where the decorative line detail has room to read.
foundry_blurb: A fresh take on Resistenza's bestselling Afrobeat from 2010, bringing a new uppercase character set and a fully redesigned, optimised lowercase. The nostalgic 70s multilinear optical graphic elements make every letter a graphic object, suited to concert posters, party flyers, CD covers and advertising – especially effective in print at display sizes.

name: Ainda
classification_notes: Multiline decorative script based on an English copperplate skeleton. The double-line construction creates a ribbon effect at connecting strokes, adding a depth illusion. Slanted axis gives it dynamism. Strictly display-weight — the multiline treatment makes it unreadable at small sizes.
summary: A decorative multiline display script that layers a double-stroke ribbon effect over a copperplate skeleton, built for large headline use only.
description: Ainda is a display script from Resistenza Type that merges a multiline stroke treatment with an English copperplate structure. The double-line construction produces a ribbon effect at the letter connections, creating an illusion of depth and perspective. It works only at large sizes, where the novelty of the technique reads clearly — at text sizes it collapses into noise.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describe Ainda as born from a long-standing affection for both multilinear type and classic script forms — a decision to bring the two together. The slanted angle is deliberate: it adds dynamism, and the ribbon effect that emerges where the lines meet in the connections gives the face a sense of depth.

name: Industria Sans
classification_notes: Modular geometric sans-serif with strong vertical axis, soft rounded corners and ink traps. Three widths (Condensed, Regular, Wide) in six weights, each with italic and "Back" alternate styles. Variable font available across weight and width axes.
summary: A modular geometric sans-serif spanning three widths and six weights, with ink traps, italic and "Back" alternate styles, and a variable font, designed by Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González for Resistenza Type.
description: Industria Sans is a geometric sans-serif built on a modular structure with strong vertical proportions, soft rounded corners and ink traps that give it a clean industrial character. The family covers Condensed, Regular and Wide widths across six weights, each with italic and decorative "Back" alternates, totalling 36 static styles alongside a full variable font. It supports Western, Central/Eastern European, Baltic, Turkish and Romanian scripts, making it a practical choice for branding, posters, packaging and editorial headlines.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describe Industria Sans as a big sans-serif family with an industrial look, modular and geometric in construction with strong vertical proportions and soft rounded corners. Designed for branding, logos, posters and headlines, it ships with OpenType features and broad European language coverage, and is available as both static fonts and a variable font.

name: Norman Stencil
classification_notes: High-contrast condensed stencil serif. Inherits Norman's narrow proportions and vertical stress; interrupted strokes throughout give the characteristic stencil appearance. Reads best at large display sizes. Not suited to text settings.
summary: The stencil counterpart to Resistenza's popular Norman serif: a narrow, high-contrast display family with interrupted strokes, available in four weights each with a matching italic.
description: Released in April 2021, Norman Stencil adapts the Norman family's condensed, high-contrast proportions into stencil form, breaking strokes at the points where a physical stencil template would need bridges. Four weights run from Regular to Fat, each paired with an italic, giving designers enough range for layered headline and identity work. It suits editorial, packaging and branding contexts where an industrial or utilitarian aesthetic is part of the brief.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describe Norman Stencil as the stencil version of their best-selling Norman – a narrow, high-contrast serif built for big text, logos, headlines and other display purposes. It includes OpenType ligatures and alternates, and is available on Adobe Fonts.

name: Dream Away
classification_notes: Casual script inspired by Italian calligraphic tradition (bella scrittura). Six weight grades in 50-unit increments from hairline to medium, plus two rough-texture variants. Long stroke connections, small apertures and counters, extended OpenType swash alternates. Designed by Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González.
summary: A casual handwritten script in six weights, drawing from Italian bella scrittura tradition, with rough-texture variants and an extended OpenType swash set for decorative emphasis.
description: Dream Away is a casual script typeface designed by Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González for Resistenza Type, released in 2022. It draws from Italian calligraphic writing, with long stroke connections and compact counters that give the letterforms a fluid, effortless quality. Six weight grades are available alongside two rough-texture cuts that lend an authentically hand-drawn feel, with OpenType swash alternates throughout for expressive typographic variation.
foundry_blurb: A handwritten script with long connections and small apertures, rooted in Italian bella scrittura tradition. The family spans six weights with an extended set of OpenType swash alternates for added emphasis, plus two rough-textured variants that capture the natural irregularity of real pen-on-paper writing.

name: Industria Serif
classification_notes: Geometric serif with a rationalist, industrial character. Upright construction is clean and structured rather than humanist. Notable for including a backslant variant alongside the standard italic across all three widths, which is unusual for the category. Variable font axes cover weight and width continuously.
summary: A 54-style geometric serif spanning three widths and six weights, with upright, italic and backslant variants throughout and a variable font covering the full weight-width range.
description: Industria Serif pairs clean geometric letterforms with the practicality of a large, well-structured type family. Three widths — Condensed, Regular and Wide — each cover a six-weight range from Thin to Bold, with both italic and backslant variants in every permutation, giving 54 static styles in total. A variable font version spans the complete weight and width range in a single file, and language support covers Western, Central and Eastern European, Baltic, Turkish and Romanian character sets.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describe Industria Serif as a modern serif with a geometric touch, built around two variable axes to give access to three distinct widths and a full weight range. The family is positioned for brand identity work requiring consistent application across print and digital formats.

name: Adore You
classification_notes: Dry-brush calligraphic script, hand-drawn by Giuseppe Salerno and digitised to preserve textured ink-on-paper strokes. Bouncy, irregular baseline typical of expressive brush lettering. Not a traditional italic-bearing type family.
summary: A dry-brush calligraphic script with textured strokes and a lively bouncy baseline, aimed at beauty, food and fashion branding.
description: Adore You is a hand-drawn brush script by Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González, digitised to retain the texture of dry ink on paper. The family ships in two main styles – Regular and Slanted – plus a set of decorative strokes and ornaments. OpenType alternates and an extended ligature set allow customisation of the expressive, natural-feeling letterforms.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza positions Adore You as a dry-brush script born from calligraphy, designed to carry the warmth of handmade lettering into brand and packaging work across beauty, food, fashion and publishing contexts.

name: Guess What
classification_notes: Felt-tip marker handwriting family designed as a four-style layerable system. Not a utility typeface; suited to decorative headlines and packaging. OpenType alternation cycles through five sets of hand-sketched glyphs to reduce mechanical repetition.
summary: A felt-tip marker display family of four styles – Regular, Inline, Papercut and Shadow – built to be layered, with OpenType randomisation cycling through five hand-sketched glyph sets to reduce mechanical repetition.
description: Guess What is drawn from five sets of letterforms sketched with a felt-tip marker, giving the family a genuinely casual, handmade character. OpenType code alternates between glyph variants automatically, sidestepping the copy-paste regularity that exposes most digital handwriting faces. The four styles are designed to stack on top of one another, producing illustrated headline effects suited to book covers, packaging and children's content.
foundry_blurb: Five sets of felt-tip marker letterforms, randomly cycled via OpenType to imitate the natural variation of handwriting. More than 1,500 glyphs across four styles – Regular, Inline, Papercut and Shadow – designed to be overlapped as layers for editorial and packaging applications.

name: Dolce Caffe
classification_notes: All-caps hand-lettered display typeface with a chalkboard aesthetic, drawn from Berlin café menu boards. Not a connected script – uppercase-only with expressive, slightly rough chalk-style strokes. Rich OpenType palette: contextual swashes, discretionary ligatures, ornaments, three stylistic sets and titling alternates.
summary: An all-caps hand-lettered display face drawn from Berlin chalkboard menus, warm and artisanal in character, suited to café branding and heritage packaging.
description: Dolce Caffe was designed by Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González in 2011, inspired by the hand-written chalkboard menus of Berlin cafés. An uppercase-only display face, it carries an expressive, slightly rough quality that works well at large sizes on signage, packaging and café collateral. The family has expanded with 3D, chalk and multiline sub-families that push its decorative range further, though all variants remain firmly in display territory.
foundry_blurb: A pretty hand-written font that is very legible and high in style, with carefully constructed all-uppercase letters. Totally inspired by the hand-written chalkboards of Berlin.

name: Annuario
classification_notes: Sans serif with brush-influenced strokes and a humanist construction. Multi-width family spanning Condensed, Regular and Expanded cuts across six weights; the brushy texture gives headlines warmth. Originally designed for calendar layout. A companion Variable version covers both weight and width axes.
summary: A humanist sans with brush-influenced strokes, originally drawn for calendar layouts, spanning three widths and six weights with full italics and a variable version.
description: Annuario started life as a typeface for calendar design and expanded into a 48-style family covering Condensed, Regular and Expanded widths across six weights from Thin to Black, each with matching italics. The letterforms carry a subtle brushy quality that gives display settings warmth without tipping into ornament. A variable version covering both weight and width axes suits editorial systems that need typographic range across breakpoints or animated headlines.
foundry_blurb: A large sans serif with a brushy character, first created for a calendar application. The family spans 48 fonts across two axes – Condensed through Expanded widths, Thin through Black weights – with full italic coverage and a companion variable font.

name: Smoothy
classification_notes: Textured brush script with urban sign-painting and hand-lettering influences. The original family carries rough brushy textures; the Pro subfamily removes the texture and introduces a Light weight. Slanted variants serve as italics. No width variants or optical sizes. OpenType ligatures and stylistic alternates included.
summary: A textured brush script drawn from urban sign-painting and hand-lettering traditions, suited to packaging, apparel graphics and display headlines.
description: Smoothy delivers rough-edged brush energy with a confident, hand-painted character that reads as spontaneous without feeling careless. The Pro subfamily strips the texture for cleaner reproduction and adds a Light weight, giving designers two distinct moods within a single family. Best at display sizes for food and cosmetic packaging, fashion labels, holiday cards and apparel.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describe Smoothy as urban, modern and sign-painting inspired – a brushy typeface for headlines, posters, invitations, apparel and packaging. The Pro version follows as a smoother, texture-free take with an additional light weight and slanted variants for greater versatility across print and digital contexts.

name: Notes Pen
classification_notes: Casual handwritten italic script simulating fluid pen-on-paper lettering. One of four instrument-specific cuts in the Notes family (Pen, Pencil, Marker, Felt Tip). No upright roman companion — the font is inherently oblique in character.
summary: A casual handwritten italic by Giuseppe Salerno that mimics fluid pen lettering, suited to captions, quick notes and informal signage.
description: Notes Pen is the calligraphic cut of Resistenza's Notes family, a handwritten italic blending typography with spontaneous pen-on-paper character. It holds up at small sizes and includes built-in ligatures to support a natural rhythm. The family spans four variants – Pen, Pencil, Marker and Felt Tip – each evoking a distinct writing instrument, sold as separate fonts.
foundry_blurb: Notes is a handwritten italic family described by Resistenza as casual and fresh. It combines typography with handwriting across four cuts differentiated by instrument character, and is recommended for publishing, quick notes, captions and signage.

name: Little Boxes
classification_notes: Handwritten display face drawn with felt pen on smooth paper, then digitised. Three stylistic variants rather than a traditional weight axis. Letterforms are optmised for legibility while preserving analogue irregularity. Sits at the casual/novelty end of the display spectrum.
summary: A three-style handwritten sans-serif drawn with felt pen on smooth paper, balancing legible letterforms with a casual, analogue warmth.
description: Little Boxes mimics felt-pen lettering on smooth paper, with subtle letterform inconsistencies that keep it feeling human. The three variants – Regular, Slanted and Dance – offer different levels of informality, with OpenType alternates extending the handcrafted effect. It suits headlines, packaging, invitations and branding where a hand-drawn, friendly tone is the point.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describe Little Boxes as a fresh, happy handwritten sans-serif conceived to create the illusion of human craft. Drawn with felt pen on smooth paper and digitised, it optimises its letterforms to maintain readability across print and digital applications while keeping the analogue character intact.

name: Groupie
classification_notes: Liberty Art Nouveau lettering fused with 1970s psychedelic poster typography. High-contrast decorative display face with curvilinear forms, OpenType alternate glyph set, and a built-in icon collection. Two stylistic variants rather than a conventional weight range.
summary: A two-style psychedelic display face that blends Art Nouveau liberty lettering with the fevered energy of 1970s concert poster typography, built for headline work where period mood is the point.
description: Groupie draws on curvilinear Art Nouveau forms and the overloaded drama of 1970s psychedelic poster type, conceived as a tribute to groupie culture. It ships in two styles – Regular and Gloss – with an OpenType panel of alternative glyphs and a built-in icon set. The use case is deliberately narrow: large-scale headlines for music, fashion or countercultural projects where the retro aesthetic is the brief.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza is co-run by Giuseppe Salerno, a trained calligrapher from Turin, and Paco González, a self-taught designer from Valencia. They work by hand first – pen and paper before pixels – drawing across the lettering traditions of Italy and Spain, and describe their output as carrying a bold, humanistic quality.

name: Hello Fresh
classification_notes: All-caps casual hand-drawn display typeface with a bouncing baseline. Not a connected script — letterforms are individual, upright or slanted, with two alternate glyph sets per style accessible via OpenType to simulate natural hand-lettered variation. Four-style family: Regular, Bold, Slanted, Bold Slanted. No true italics; Slanted styles are obliques.
summary: Hello Fresh is an all-caps casual hand-lettered display family with a bouncing baseline and OpenType alternate glyphs, suited to food packaging, labels and artisanal branding.
description: Designed by Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González of Resistenza, Hello Fresh is a four-style hand-drawn all-caps family — Regular, Bold, Slanted and Bold Slanted — each carrying two alternate glyph sets to vary texture across repeated characters. Its bouncy, informal baseline gives it a natural hand-lettered quality without the connecting strokes of a true script. Best suited to food packaging, holiday cards, fashion labels and invitations; too decorative for body text or sustained reading.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza pitches Hello Fresh as a font where freshness meets fun, pairing a lively bouncing energy with dual glyph sets per style so designers can mix and match letterforms for a natural hand-crafted feel. Suggested applications include packaging, labels, books, invitations, wrapping paper, T-shirts and fashion goods.

name: Mina
classification_notes: Connected calligraphic script with variable stroke weight and long elastic letter connections. Inspired by 1950s Mediterranean lettering tradition. Inherently slanted by nature – no separate roman/italic distinction. Multiple subfamilies extend the system into decorative and shadow territory.
summary: A calligraphic connected script from Resistenza with long elastic strokes and a relaxed 1950s Mediterranean character, spanning nine weights plus Calligraphic, Shadow and Noodle sub-families.
description: Mina is a connected calligraphic script designed by Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González, released in 2013. It draws on Mediterranean lettering traditions, with flowing elastic connections between letters and clean thin strokes that hold up across a broad weight range from Thin to Super. With 515 glyphs and extensive OpenType features – swashes, ligatures, alternates, initial and final forms – it suits logotypes, editorial titles and boutique branding but has limited utility in body text or neutral UI work.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describes Mina as capturing the feel of calligraphy in a relaxed cursive with long elastic letter connections and clean, thin lines. The family spans from light to heavy with Calligraphic and Shadow variants, designed to work individually or in combination. It includes many loop options for per-letter customisation and is available on Adobe Fonts.

name: Timberline
classification_notes: Single-weight casual brush script drawn with a felt pen on smooth paper and digitised to preserve the texture of hand-made strokes. OpenType stylistic alternates and an extended ligatures set provide some letterform variety without additional cuts. A companion icon set (Timberline Icons) ships separately with ornaments, catchwords and swashes.
summary: A single-weight casual brush script drawn with felt pen on paper and digitised to preserve the texture of hand-made strokes.
description: Timberline is a brush script drawn with a felt pen on smooth paper, then digitised to retain the textured, hand-made quality of the original marks. It ships in one weight with OpenType stylistic alternates and an extended ligatures set, giving typographic variety without additional cuts. Real-world use includes the Carrie Underwood "Cry Pretty" album cover and a Scorpions lyrics video, placing it squarely in music and entertainment branding.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describes Timberline as a handwriting-style font full of character, with textured lines and graceful strokes drawn using a felt brush pen and digitised to capture the realness of hand-made marks. It is offered as a casual script for design applications, paired with Timberline Icons – a companion set of catchwords, ornaments, swashes and doodles for layout customisation.

name: Videomusic
classification_notes: Bubble display typeface with pointed edges and a subtle forward inclination, referencing the lettering aesthetic of 80s music television channels. Five complementary styles (Regular, Thick, Bubble, Outline, Shadow) designed for layering. No true italic or condensed cuts. Classified "script" on some reseller catalogues but the design is properly a decorative display family.
summary: A five-style bubble display family drawing on 80s music television lettering, with layerable Regular, Thick, Bubble, Outline and Shadow cuts for loud headline work.
description: Videomusic takes its cues from the pointed, angled lettering seen on 80s music television channels and pop culture graphics. The family ships five complementary styles – Regular, Thick, Bubble, Outline and Shadow – designed to be stacked and combined for bold headline treatments. Its appeal sits firmly within retro music and entertainment branding, with little crossover utility outside that register.
foundry_blurb: A bubble font based on POP culture letterings from the eighties. The edges carry a pointed shape with subtle inclination giving the dynamic quality associated with music television from that era. All five fonts can be layered together to create striking composite artworks.

name: Newland
classification_notes: Three-variant display family modelled on Rudolf Koch's 1923 Neuland. Shares the blocky, hand-carved woodcut character of the original with no weight axis. Variants differ in texture (clean, weathered, rounded) rather than weight. No italic; all-caps sensibility. Designer duo: Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González.
summary: A blocky all-caps display family drawing directly from Rudolf Koch's 1923 Neuland, offered in three texture-driven variants: Regular, Rough and Rounded.
description: Newland is a three-variant display family released in 2014 by Resistenza Type designers Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González. Each variant shares the same chunky, calligraphic-stroke DNA inherited from Koch's Neuland but differs in finish: Regular delivers clean, confident edges; Rough adds a weathered, handcrafted grain; Rounded softens corners into a more approachable silhouette. It suits headline, poster and logo work where bold graphic impact matters, but the narrow stylistic brief limits broader use.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describes Newland as a blocky uppercase family inspired by Rudolf Koch's calligraphic Neuland. Regular offers defined edges and balanced proportions; Rounded smooths those into gentler curves; Rough introduces the marks of imperfection and a weathered, handcrafted feel. Recommended for branding, editorial headlines, packaging and vintage-themed projects.

name: Shabby Chic
classification_notes: Single-weight dry brush charm script developed from Resistenza's monolinear script Mina. Heavy distressing and long letter connections give an organic, hand-crafted quality. No weight range, no italics, no width variants.
summary: A single-weight dry brush charm script with distressed edges and flowing letter connections, built for warm, artisan-flavoured cards, labels and print collateral.
description: Shabby Chic is drawn with a dry brush pen to mimic a weathered, hand-made sign, with distressed edges and long letter connections giving it an organic, nostalgic feel. OpenType alternates, ligatures and initial/final forms allow limited customisation within its single Regular cut. Its appeal is narrow – it works well for invitations, labels and artisan branding, but the single weight and decorative character make it unsuitable for running text or varied typographic hierarchies.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describes Shabby Chic as capturing the spirit of the Shabby Chic design aesthetic: softened, distressed edges that convey age, warmth and authenticity, yielding a soft, relaxed and romantic feeling suited to intimate, handcrafted communication.

name: Royale
classification_notes: Monoline Tuscan display with bifurcated decorative serifs and rounded terminals, drawing directly from Victorian-era display typography. Designed to be layered across widths for polychromatic effects. Not a revival — a contemporary reinterpretation of the genre with a warmer, more playful register.
summary: A monoline Victorian Tuscan display face with bifurcated serifs and eight layerable weights across four widths, including Condensed, Compressed, Italic, Rough, Outline and Shadow cuts.
description: Royale reinvents the bifurcated Tuscan genre with a monoline construction, rounded terminals and elaborate decorative spurs drawn from Victorian-era display printing. The family spans eight numerically named weights across at least three widths — Regular, Condensed and Compressed — with italic variants and special styles (Outline, Shadow, Rough) designed to be stacked for polychromatic effects. Designed by Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González, it suits poster work, packaging and heritage-inflected branding where period character is the brief.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describe Royale as a contemporary reinvention of the bifurcated Tuscan genre in warm and playful form. Rounded terminals and elaborate spurs sit within a monoline structure; the eight weights and multiple widths are designed to be layered, recreating the polychromatic display effects of Victorian-era printing.

name: Respect
classification_notes: Brush script inspired by sign painting and brush pen calligraphy traditions. Slanted angles and curved strokes with a street art and hand lettering sensibility. OpenType swash alternates available. Four weights from Regular to Black, no italics or width variants.
summary: A bold brush script in four weights, drawing on sign painting and brush pen calligraphy, with slanted angles, curved strokes and OpenType swash alternates.
description: Respect is a brush script family from Resistenza designers Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González, released in 2016. The four weights – Regular through Black – share slanted angles and curved strokes rooted in sign painting and hand lettering traditions, with a street art edge that makes the family well-suited to expressive logo work, posters and packaging. OpenType features unlock swash alternates for added personality.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describe Respect as their tribute to hand lettering culture, drawing on the traditional craft of sign painting and brush pen calligraphy. The foundry blends that heritage with contemporary street art influence, using slanted angles and curved stems to deliver what they call active energy, plenty of attitude and a courageous character.

name: Nautica Lines
classification_notes: Monolinear script rooted in copperplate calligraphy but rendered without thick-thin contrast, emulating the consistent stroke of a rollerball pen. Comes in two terminal-style subfamilies (Line with flat ends, Noodle with rounded ends) across five numbered weight steps. Display-only — not intended for body text.
summary: A monolinear calligraphic script in five weight steps, offered in flat-terminal Line and rounded-terminal Noodle variants, drawn from copperplate tradition but executed with rollerball-pen consistency.
description: Nautica Lines strips copperplate calligraphy back to a single-stroke approach, removing all thick-thin contrast for a clean, even line weight throughout. Five numbered weights — from fine to bold — allow designers to match stroke weight to reproduction scale, whether small label copy or large headline use. The Noodle subfamily softens the aesthetic with rounded terminals; the Line subfamily ends flat for a crisper, more restrained look.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza present Nautica Lines as a more delicate companion to their Nautica typeface — a monolinear script channelling copperplate grace through the precision of a rollerball pen. Ten fonts pair Line and Noodle variants across five weight steps, with OpenType contextual alternates, standard ligatures and stylistic sets for typographic control.

name: Nostalgia
classification_notes: Serif in construction but firmly display in application – rounded, softened terminals and a heavy swash/alternate set make it unsuitable for body text. The three-font package comprises one display typeface (Regular) plus two decorative companions: Effect (a layering/luminous overlay font) and Flowers (a dingbat ornament set). Draws from 1970s graphic design and retro lettering conventions.
summary: A 1970s-inspired display serif with soft rounded terminals, an extended swash and alternate set, and two companion decorative fonts for layered vintage compositions.
description: Nostalgia is a display serif designed by Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González of Resistenza, released in April 2020. It takes 1970s letterform conventions as its starting point, applying rounded, softened terminals to create a warm, nostalgic character suited to headlines, logos and wedding stationery. The three-font family adds an Effect overlay for luminous layering and a Flowers dingbat set for ornamental flourishes, extending the visual vocabulary of the package beyond the base typeface.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza positions Nostalgia as a contemporary take on vintage letterforms, with softened edges and rounded terminations designed to convey a positive mood. An extended set of alternates and swashes, accessible via OpenType, enables varied lettering compositions; combining the main font with the Effect companion adds a luminous, retro-print quality, while the Flowers set provides decorative florals and ornamental forms. The foundry pitches the family across a broad range of applications, from logos and magazine covers to wedding cards and posters.

name: Stencil Creek
classification_notes: Rounded stencil display typeface influenced by classic sans serifs and North West Pacific street signage. Uses a numeric weight-naming convention (005–070) rather than conventional descriptors. Stencil apertures are built into all letterforms across the family. Rough texture variants available at two of the heavier weights.
summary: A rounded stencil display face rooted in North West Pacific street signage, spanning eight numerically named weights plus two rough-textured variants.
description: Stencil Creek draws from the vernacular of North West Pacific street signs, rendered as a rounded stencil form influenced by classic sans serifs. The family runs from 005 to 070 across eight weights, with Rough variants at 50 and 70 adding a worn, textured quality. Weights can be overlapped to produce an inline layering effect, and the set includes OpenType swashes and alternates.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza is an Italian-Spanish type studio run by Giuseppe Salerno, a trained calligrapher from Torino, and Paco González, a self-taught designer from Valencia. The foundry works by hand first, using pen and paper before moving to digital, with the aim of producing type that carries a humanistic, place-connected quality.

name: Story Tales
classification_notes: Display typeface with strong 1970s book-cover character, drawing on Victorian decorative type, 60s psychedelia and post-war children's publishing. Designed as a layering system rather than a conventional weight-based family. All variants are intended to stack for chromatic effects. Slanted styles are obliques, not true italics.
summary: A 1970s book-cover-inspired display family with ten stackable styles built for chromatic layering on fairy-tale, fantasy and retro editorial work.
description: Story Tales draws on 1970s book cover design, 60s psychedelia, Victorian decorative typography and post-war children's almanacks to create a whimsical display family. Its ten styles -- covering inline, slanted, ornamental and textural variants -- are designed to stack on top of one another, enabling polychromatic effects from a single purchase. The family is tightly scoped to fairy-tale, fantasy and retro-themed contexts; outside those registers it has little to offer.
foundry_blurb: Story Tales is a type family for wondrous, romantic and playful narratives, drawing on 70s book covers, 60s flower power, Victorian chromatic type and post-war children's publications. Eight stackable core styles -- plus ornamental and textural supplements -- let designers build striking multi-colour headline typography without needing separate font files.

name: Starburst
classification_notes: Single-style expressive calligraphic script drawn with an oblique nib, emulating copperplate traditions with pressure-varied, gestural strokes. No weight range, no italic variant separate from the inherent oblique character of the letterforms.
summary: A single-style gestural calligraphic script drawn with an oblique nib, blending copperplate precision with pressure-varied, expressive strokes.
description: Starburst is a light calligraphic script by Giuseppe Salerno, built from hand-sketched strokes using an oblique nib for copperplate and pencil work. The design plays with pressure and angle to produce a dynamic, rhythmical flow that sits between formal copperplate and freehand expressiveness. With a single Regular weight, it suits headline and display contexts where calligraphic character is the main draw.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describes Starburst as a gestural light script drawn with an oblique nib, interpreting expressive energetic calligraphy through shifting pressures and angles, with every stroke originally sketched by hand. They position it as a fusion between calligraphy and typography, rhythmical and full of grace.

name: Beach Please
classification_notes: Handwritten brush script drawn with a pointed brush and watercolour technique, inspired by mid-century sign painting. The base script includes extensive OpenType alternates, swashes and ligatures. The Caps and Wide variants introduce reversed contrast on certain letterforms, which shifts their feel closer to display lettering than conventional script. Slanted variants serve as oblique counterparts throughout. An Icons style adds tropical/vintage illustrations, making this a themed novelty family rather than a general-purpose script.
summary: A summer-flavoured brush script family by Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González, spanning a flowing sign-painting script, reversed-contrast caps and wide variants, slanted counterparts, and a tropical icon set.
description: Beach Please is a handwritten brush script inspired by mid-century sign painting, with exaggerated curves and lively punctuation giving it an easy, warm-weather energy. The Caps and Wide variants apply reversed contrast to selected letterforms, making them more suited to punchy headlines than flowing text. An Icons style adds a set of hand-drawn tropical and fruity illustrations, keeping the whole family firmly in seasonal promotional territory.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describe Beach Please as a relaxed brush font built with pointed brush and watercolour technique, distilling the spirit of sign painting with a fun, fresh twist on certain curves and punctuation. The script style leans on rich OpenType alternates, swashes and ligatures to sustain a realistic handwritten quality; the Caps and Wide styles exploit reversed contrast for headline impact. A set of sketchy vintage-style tropical icons rounds out the family.

name: Vermouth
classification_notes: Sans-serif letterforms engineered as a layered display system; high stroke contrast between thick and thin variants; inspired by mid-century Italian hand-painted signage. Not intended for text setting.
summary: A layered display family of 8 styles built for stacking colour and depth effects, drawn from mid-century Italian sign-painting.
