description: Vermouth draws on the bold lettered signage of 1960s Italy, offering eight complementary styles – thick, thin, outlined and "tipsy" bouncing variants – designed to be overlaid for dimensional colour effects. The sans-serif letterforms carry high stroke contrast and a confident vintage energy, suiting headlines, packaging and retro branding work. It ships without italics or width variants and functions strictly as a display tool.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza Type is an independent foundry founded by Giuseppe Salerno, a trained calligrapher from Turin, and Paco González, a self-taught designer from Valencia. They produce retail and custom typefaces oriented towards branding and editorial use.

name: Suerte
classification_notes: Display typeface with inverted contrast (horizontal strokes heavier than verticals) and bifurcated Tuscan serifs, drawing on Caslon's Italian type and Aldo Novarese's Estro for the Nebiolo foundry. Letterforms were drawn with a flat brush and Indian ink before vectorisation. Ten stylistic variants cover clean, roughened, inline, outline and shadow treatments, each paired with an italic. Includes a supplementary dingbats and icons set.
summary: A brush-drawn Tuscan display typeface with inverted contrast and bifurcated serifs, reviving the idiom of 19th-century Italian wood type through ten stylistic variants.
description: Suerte takes its cues from Caslon's Italian type and Aldo Novarese's Estro, translating that tradition into ten variants – Regular, Rough, Lines, Outline and Shadow, each paired with an italic. Designed by Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González, the letterforms were first drawn with a flat brush and Indian ink then vectorised, retaining handmade texture. The family also includes a set of dingbats and icons, making it best suited to poster headlines, packaging and decorative signage.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza Type is a digital independent foundry run by Giuseppe Salerno, a Turin-trained calligrapher, and Paco González, a self-taught Spanish designer from Valencia. The studio produces Latin display and text typefaces grounded in historical printing traditions and calligraphic practice.

name: Auster
classification_notes: Reverse contrast humanist sans-serif: horizontal strokes are deliberately heavier than the verticals, inverting the normal stress convention. The forms originated as hand-painted letterforms using a flat brush, then refined on tracing paper before digitisation. The result sits somewhere between a sturdy text sans and a personality-led display face.
summary: A 20-style reverse-contrast sans-serif with genuine craft behind it, born from hand-painted letterforms at the TipoBrda workshop in Slovenia and refined over three years by Resistenza's two founders.
description: Auster inverts the standard stroke logic of a sans-serif – horizontal strokes are thicker than the verticals – giving it a confident, slightly idiosyncratic character without tipping into novelty. Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González spent three years on it, starting with a flat brush, moving to pencil on tracing paper, then to careful digitisation, and the handmade origin shows in how the curves sit. The 10-weight range with full italics and a variable version makes it adaptable, though the reverse contrast means it reads best at headline or medium-display sizes rather than long body copy.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza is an Italian type studio co-founded by Giuseppe Salerno, a trained calligrapher from Torino, and Paco González, a self-taught designer from Valencia. They bridge traditional pen-and-paper craft with digital type production, and the results tend to carry a tactile, handmade quality rare in commercial sans-serif releases.

name: Blaq
classification_notes: Ornamental blackletter based on Henry W. Troy's Trojan Text. Draws on the Victorian Gothic revival tradition that originated in 1740s England. Bold strokes, dramatic contrast and decorative embellishments place it firmly in the display/headline blackletter tradition rather than the liturgical Textura or chancery Fraktur streams.
summary: A Victorian Gothic blackletter in two styles – Regular and Rough – drawn from Henry W. Troy's Trojan Text and suited to headlines and period-styled design work.
description: Blaq is an ornamental blackletter typeface from Resistenza Type, inspired by Henry W. Troy's Trojan Text and the Gothic revival movement that spread through architecture and decorative arts from the 1740s onwards. Its two styles – Regular and Rough – share bold strokes, dramatic contrast and Victorian embellishments that suit headline work, poster design and period-influenced branding. The family is narrow in scope: two weights, no italics, and a character set covering Western European languages.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describe Blaq as a contemporary take on Trojan Text, drawing on Neo-Gothic design principles from 1740s England and the Victorian era's extension of Gothic style into the decorative arts. The foundry positions it as a headline and display typeface that works in design settings requiring historical character.

name: DreamTeam
classification_notes: Multiline (inline) display typeface. Modular letterforms with long limbs and deliberate shifts in stroke weight that create a sense of directional movement. The doubled-line construction gives it a graphic, layered quality typical of sport and athleisure lettering traditions.
summary: A four-style multiline display family with modular letterforms and a kinetic, sport-inflected character suited to headlines, signage and athleisure branding.
description: DreamTeam is a multiline display typeface released by Resistenza in 2018, designed by Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González. Its modular letterforms feature long limbs and shifting stroke weight, giving text a strong sense of directional movement and speed. The four styles – Regular, Italic, Thicker and Thicker Italic – cover the main display weight range without any width variants.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describes DreamTeam as a multiline display font inspired by their bestseller Afrobeat, noting its long limbs, nimble movement and shifting weight make it perfect for grabbing attention across signage, print advertising, editorial applications such as book covers, and athleisure apparel.

name: Mela Pro
classification_notes: Handmade pointed brush script with high contrast and thick calligraphic strokes, designed to evoke urban fat-marker lettering with calligraphic refinement. Single weight/style; the "Pro" suffix denotes extended character set rather than a weight variant.
summary: A pointed-brush script drawn with walnut ink by Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González, blending calligraphic contrast with an urban fat-marker aesthetic across 473 glyphs including ligatures, alternates and ornaments.
description: Created with a pointed brush and walnut ink, Mela Pro pairs the stroke contrast of calligraphic letterforms with the thick weight of urban street lettering. The Pro edition expands the basic Mela character set to 473 glyphs, adding alternates, OpenType ligatures, icons and ornaments for flexible display layouts. Best suited to headlines, packaging, posters and branding where a handcrafted, high-contrast brush aesthetic is the point.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describe Mela Pro as a handmade typeface that combines calligraphic shapes and strokes with a modern urban style, delivering thick brushstrokes with a refined and elegant touch. The extended character set allows designers to personalise layouts via OpenType ligatures and alternates, with suggested uses spanning magazines, packaging, advertising, branding, posters, editorials, TV, film and websites.

name: Dolce Caffe Chalk
classification_notes: Chalk-textured hand-lettered family, classified as both Script and Display by major distributors. The regular ("Chalk") is an upright casual roman; Script is a flowing connected hand; Extras provides swashes, ornaments and icons. Drawn with crayons on paper rather than a brush or stylus, giving it a distinctive dry, rough texture.
summary: A chalk-textured hand-lettered family of four styles drawn with crayons on paper, suited to artisanal packaging, seasonal cards and label design.
description: Dolce Caffe Chalk is the chalk-textured companion to Resistenza's Dolce Caffè, its four styles drawn by hand with crayons on paper to produce authentic rough texturing. The family spans an upright roman, an italic, a flowing connected script and an extras set of swashes, ornaments and icons. It works best at display sizes for labels, food and cosmetics packaging, invitations and festive graphics where informality and warmth are the brief.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describe the family as "perfectly imperfect" – drawn with crayons on paper specifically to capture the roughness and warmth of real chalk lettering. Recommended for seasonal packaging, artisanal product labels, DIY artwork and holiday cards, and suggested as a pairing with their Gessetto typeface.

name: Glob
classification_notes: All-caps bubble-letter display font. Inflated, rounded letterforms with strong cartoon character. Six stylistic variants span clean, outline and rough treatments, each with a matching italic cut. No weight axis; variation is purely stylistic.
summary: A bubble-letter display font with chunky, inflated letterforms available in six variants covering clean, outline and rough treatments, each with an italic cut.
description: Glob commits fully to the bubble-letter aesthetic: rounded, air-filled letterforms with strong cartoon energy and no concession to restraint. Six variants – regular, italic, outline, italic outline, rough and italic rough – give it more internal range than most novelty fonts of this type. Its use cases are narrow: children's media, sports branding, posters and packaging where bold playfulness is the explicit brief.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describes Glob as a multilanguage bubble-letter font that includes italic, outline and rough versions.

name: Pando Script
classification_notes: Display brush script with deliberately inverted stroke contrast — thicker strokes where convention would place the thin, and vice versa. Four stylistic variants rather than a traditional weight range. Slanted styles function as the oblique counterparts.
summary: A display brush script with inverted stroke contrast, available in four stylistic variants and loaded with ligatures and alternates for branding and headline use.
description: Pando Script subverts the usual brush script formula by reversing the expected stroke contrast — the thick strokes fall where you'd expect thin ones, giving it an angular, graphic character. It comes in four variants (Regular, Regular II, Slanted, Slanted II), where the "II" cuts likely default to different stylistic alternates. The family suits headlines, labels, packaging and identity work, but its narrow decorative register limits broader application.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describes Pando Script as a brush script with inverted contrast and a lot of personality, packed with ligatures and alternates, and recommended for headlines, labels, packaging and branding.

name: Tresor
classification_notes: High-contrast display sans-serif with a romantic, nostalgic character. Built around contrast rather than strict geometric or humanist principles. Very light weight range (100–400 only); the ornamental emphasis — extensive swashes, alternates, ligatures — places it firmly in display territory despite the sans-serif skeleton.
summary: A high-contrast display sans-serif with a romantic edge, offering three weights with italics and over 1,000 glyphs of decorative swashes, alternates and ligatures via OpenType.
description: Tresor — French for "treasure" — is a display sans-serif by Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González, built on controlled contrast and what the foundry calls lo-fi nostalgia. The family spans three weights (100 through 400), each with a matching italic, and ships with an extensive set of ornamental alternates, swashes and ligatures accessible through OpenType features. It suits headline work, brand identities, packaging and stationery rather than body copy, and the weight range is too light for most text applications.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza positions Tresor as a family that lives up to its name: the glyphs include swashes and alternates described as jewels adorning a crown. They highlight the mix of classic proportions with a romantic twist, and recommend it for headlines, wedding invitations, packaging and social media graphics.

name: Apero Slab
classification_notes: Hand-drawn slab serif with organic, informal letterforms across five weights (Regular to Heavy), plus two decorative inline/lines effect cuts. No italics. Part of the broader Apero superfamily, which includes an accompanying sans-serif companion. Release date August 2016.
summary: A hand-lettered slab serif in five weights inspired by Turin's aperitivo tradition, with two decorative inline effects.
description: Apero Slab is a cheerful hand-drawn slab serif designed by Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González, released in 2016. It spans five weights from Regular to Heavy, with two additional Lines cuts adding a decorative inline effect to the Bold and Heavy styles. The organic letterforms suit lifestyle branding, menu design and display headlines, though the handwritten character limits its range beyond those contexts.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describes the Apero family as handmade, friendly and classy – eight fonts comprising five slab weights, two slab effects and a sans serif companion, all inspired by the aperitivo tradition in Turin.

name: Batticuore
classification_notes: Brush-based script family in two distinct variant groups: Regular (lowercase-style script) and Caps (all-caps script). Each group comes in upright, Slanted and Backslanted cuts; a Shadow style rounds out the seven-cut family. Letterforms are grounded in confident brushwork with light contrast, supplemented by extensive OpenType ligatures and alternates.
summary: A brush script family in two variant groups, Regular and Caps, each available in upright, slanted and backslanted cuts, with a Shadow style and generous OpenType ligatures and alternates throughout.
description: Designed by Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González and released in 2019, Batticuore takes its name from the Italian word for heartbeat. The seven-style family spans Regular and Caps script variants in upright, slanted and backslanted orientations, all built on confident brushwork with subtle contrast. A large set of OpenType ligatures and alternates gives designers room to personalise the lettering, making it a useful tool for logos, packaging and editorial display work.
foundry_blurb: Batticuore means palpitation in Italian. Built on brush lettering, the family offers Regular and Caps script variants, each grounded in brushstrokes with a touch of contrast and supported by a substantial set of OpenType ligatures and alternates.

name: Mina Chic
classification_notes: Calligraphic script with pointed-pen stroke contrast evolved from the monoline Mina. Features long connections, smooth swashes, and extensive OpenType alternates. Two weights only. Inspired by French New Wave cinema and 1960s pop aesthetics.
summary: A refined pointed-pen calligraphic script with French New Wave inflections, 515 glyphs and two weights, built for wedding stationery, fashion and luxury packaging.
description: Mina Chic is a calligraphic script evolved from Resistenza's earlier monoline Mina, adding pointed-nib stroke contrast, long connections and smooth swashes. It ships in two weights – Regular and Extra – and its 515 glyphs cover swashes, ligatures, alternates, and initial and final forms accessed via OpenType. The family is a natural fit for wedding stationery, wine labels, cosmetics and fashion contexts where a refined handwritten feel is wanted.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describe Mina Chic as "fresh, elegant and sexy," drawing on French Riviera aesthetics and 1960s French cinema. They position it as a refined successor to Mina, with calligraphic stroke expansion and an "authentic handmade look," and recommend it for wedding and birthday cards, invitations, wine labels, food packaging, cosmetics and poetry.

name: Mentha
classification_notes: Condensed brush pen script with looped terminals and extensive OpenType swash alternates. Not a calligraphic script in the formal sense — the influence is small brush pen, giving it a slightly informal, contemporary feel with strong upstrokes.
summary: A condensed brush pen script by Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González, with looped terminals, an extensive swash set and two weights optimised for display and packaging work.
description: Mentha is a condensed script built around small brush pen technique, with pressure-and-release strokes producing strong letterforms with distinctive loops at the ends of certain characters. Two weights cover most display needs: Regular for headlines and decorative applications, Medium adding a hairline supplementary stroke for improved legibility when set at smaller sizes. Its condensed proportions and generous swash alternates suit brand identity, packaging and editorial display, but the script nature limits its range beyond those contexts.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describe Mentha as a highly flexible script shaped by the energy of small brush pens, with swash variants and a condensed form intended to give designs a fresh, original character. The recommended pairing is their own Turquoise typeface.

name: Gessetto
classification_notes: Decorative chalk-effect display family spanning script, roman, all-caps high-contrast sans variants, cursive and backslanted styles, plus figures and ornamental cuts. Simulates handcrafted chalkboard lettering through textured strokes. No traditional weight axis; variety comes from stylistic genre shifts rather than weight steps.
summary: A nine-style chalk display family spanning script, roman, high-contrast sans variants and ornamental cuts, built to replicate authentic chalkboard lettering for signage and editorial use.
description: Gessetto is an extensive chalk-effect display family released in 2017 by Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González of Resistenza Type. Its nine cuts range from a swashy script with capital swash alternates to all-caps high-contrast sans variants, a roman, cursive and backslanted styles, plus dedicated figure and ornament sets. The family suits signage, book covers and branding work where a handcrafted chalkboard aesthetic is the deliberate goal.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza set out to capture the texture and rhythm of real chalk on board, combining varied typographic genres – script, roman, sans, figures and ornaments – so designers can mix styles within a single coherent chalk visual language.

name: PestoFresco
classification_notes: Handwritten lettering system with deliberate imperfections and an artisanal character. Technically described as sans-serif but functions as a decorative display type with 28 fonts spanning structural weights and novelty overlay styles. Designed for large-scale use in packaging and lifestyle branding rather than body text.
summary: A 28-style handwritten lettering system from Resistenza, built around artisanal imperfection, offering structural weights with rough and italic variants plus an extensive range of decorative overlay fonts for packaging and lifestyle branding.
description: PestoFresco is designed by Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González of Resistenza Type, drawing on hand-lettered aesthetics with deliberate roughness and warmth. The family spans 28 fonts: structural weights from Thin to Regular with italic and rough variants, plus a collection of decorative overlay styles including dots, leaves, flowers, shadows and novelty decorations intended to be layered for graphic effects via OpenType. It suits food packaging, artisan product branding and editorial contexts where hand-crafted character is the primary goal.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describes PestoFresco as a lettering system that brings the warmth and authenticity of handmade typography into digital contexts, with overlapping decorative fonts designed for graphic layering and an artisanal DIY quality suited to packaging, brand identity and advertising.

name: Voguing
classification_notes: Geometric sans skeleton with multiline parallel strokes whose direction is manipulated to produce a 3D optical effect. Three directional variants (upright, slanted, backslanted) rather than a conventional weight or width range. Inspired by 1980s-90s New York ballroom culture; decorative and legible only at large sizes.
summary: A three-variant display face built from multiline strokes that shift direction to suggest 3D movement, drawing from the energy of 1980s-90s New York ballroom voguing culture.
description: Voguing takes the glamour and physicality of the New York ballroom scene and translates it into letterform: each glyph is constructed from parallel multiline strokes whose angle varies to create the illusion of three-dimensional motion. The family comes in three variants – regular, slanted and backslanted – each pushing the sense of directional energy in a different way. OpenType ligatures extend the customisation options, but the face is firmly a display tool, suited to headlines, posters and fashion branding rather than running text.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza positions Voguing as a spiritual sibling to their debut release Afrobeat, sharing the multiline construction but redirecting the strokes to achieve a 3D effect that captures the movement and self-expression of voguing. Recommended for fashion, publishing, cosmetics, sports and art contexts; best deployed in headlines, branding, magazine layouts, social media graphics and poster work.

name: MonsterHand
classification_notes: Unicase ruling-pen calligraphic display typeface with extreme stroke contrast and authentic ink texture. Sits between script and display — classified as display due to its headline-only utility and dramatic visual personality rather than traditional connected script flow. The ruling pen technique produces highly expressive letterforms with handcrafted character.
summary: A ruling-pen calligraphic display typeface with dramatic stroke contrast and authentic ink texture, drawn from Giuseppe Salerno's own handwriting.
description: MonsterHand is a unicase display typeface drawn with a ruling pen — a tool more common in technical draughtsmanship than type design — giving its letterforms an unusual, highly expressive quality. Stroke contrast is extreme and ink texture is visible at display sizes, making it a strong fit for logotypes, packaging headlines and editorial pull quotes. A single Regular weight limits its versatility considerably; this is a one-trick typeface, and the trick needs to be exactly right for the brief.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describes MonsterHand as their first ruling-pen typeface, built from Giuseppe Salerno's handwriting with expressive contrast and raw ink texture, and packaged alongside a complementary icon set.

name: La Bodeguita
classification_notes: Spencerian-influenced pointed-nib script drawn with walnut ink on an oblique penholder. Three styles rather than a conventional weight range: Regular, Slanted (an oblique variant, not a true italic), and Swashes (decorative alternate glyphs). No width variants, no optical sizes, no condensed cuts.
summary: A Spencerian pointed-nib script drawn with walnut ink, built for wine labels, food packaging and luxury brand work where handcrafted provenance is the point.
description: La Bodeguita is a calligraphic script drawn by Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González using a Spencerian feather on an oblique penholder and walnut ink, producing soft, flowing letterforms with genuine pen character. The family ships as three styles – Regular, Slanted and Swashes – with over 400 glyphs, giving designers room to build varied lettering compositions. Its name nods to the bodega, and its natural home is wine and spirits labels, fine food packaging and anywhere a brand leans on craft and origin.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describes La Bodeguita as a soft and harmonious pointed-nib font drawn with walnut ink and a Spencerian feather on an oblique penholder, designed to bring true calligraphic elegance to label and packaging work.

name: Lovewins
classification_notes: Not a conventional alphabetic typeface. A set of 60 fixed calligraphic phrase graphics drawn with pens, brushes and other calligraphic tools, producing varied script aesthetics across the collection. Closer to a clip-art dingbat font than a composable typeface system.
summary: A collection of 60 calligraphic Pride phrases by Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González, each handlettered with different tools to produce varied script aesthetics for signage, apparel and celebration materials.
description: Lovewins is not a composable typeface but a fixed set of 60 hand-lettered phrases celebrating diversity and equal rights, drawn using various calligraphic pens and brushes that give each phrase its own distinct visual character. Released in 2017 and inspired by Madrid's World Pride, the collection is aimed squarely at Pride signage, t-shirts, stickers, posters and banners. Its scope is deliberately narrow: the glyphs are complete phrase graphics rather than individual letterforms, which limits any general typographic application.
foundry_blurb: A series of 60 phrases handwritten with expertise and love, specially designed to celebrate diversity. The lettering was crafted with different calligraphic tools creating diverse aesthetics – intended for Pride celebrations and for everyday use in promoting love and freedom.

name: Quaderno
classification_notes: Monolinear upright connected script drawing on Italian Bella Scrittura and early 20th-century French commercial lettering. The numeric weight naming system (2 through 33) denotes stroke thickness progression rather than conventional weight names. A Calligraphic sub-style references flat-nib technique; Noodle sub-styles are bolder, rounded variants. A companion family, Quaderno Slanted, provides oblique versions of all styles and is sold separately.
summary: A monolinear upright connected script drawing on Italian Bella Scrittura and early 20th-century commercial lettering, suited to children's publishing, educational materials, and display headlines.
description: Quaderno merges Italian Bella Scrittura with French script traditions into a connected, monolinear upright letterform that reads as both vernacular and considered. The numeric weight system – from 2 to 33 – gives fine-grained control over stroke thickness, while the Calligraphic and Noodle sub-families extend the range into flat-nib and expressive territory. Its natural home is children's books, educational materials, and display headlines where a handwritten warmth is the point.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describe Quaderno as a light, monolinear upright script that blends Italian and French script traditions, evoking vernacular and commercial lettering of the 20th century. It is positioned for middle-length texts, headlines, school materials, and children's book and publishing projects.

name: Bratislove
classification_notes: Casual handwritten script with a monoline character throughout. The name blends Bratislava with "love", referencing the city where it was conceived. Two italic weights (regular and bold) share a spontaneous, flowing character; a third Calligraphic cut shifts to a flat-tip marker sensibility, making it stylistically distinct within the family. All cuts lean into the slanted, dynamic letterforms typical of informal Latin scripts.
summary: A casual monoline script conceived in Bratislava, with italic and bold italic cuts plus a flat-tip calligraphic variant, suited to branding and packaging that call for personality over formality.
description: Bratislove is a handwritten script designed by Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González, released in 2012, whose name fuses Bratislava with love in a nod to its origins. The family spans two italic weights sharing a spontaneous, flowing monoline character, with a third Calligraphic cut drawn on a flat-tip marker sensibility that leans more urban and youthful than traditional calligraphy. OpenType ligatures help characters connect naturally, lending the text a convincingly handwritten flow.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describe Bratislove as a whimsical and lively collection designed to infuse projects with charm and personality, with letterforms that carry a sense of spontaneity and a fresh rhythmic quality. The Calligraphic cut takes its cue from text written with a flat-tip marker pen, offering an urban alternative to more formal calligraphic styles.

name: Dolcissimo
classification_notes: Geometric sans-serif skeleton drawn with a deliberate hand-made quality. Designed as a layered type system: base weights (Thin, Regular, Rough, Outline, Script) are intended to be overlaid with decorative fills — dots, flowers, stars, triangles and so on — to build dimensional, multi-layer compositions. The Script sub-style shifts into informal handwritten territory.
summary: A friendly geometric display sans built as a 28-style layered system, with base weights designed to be stacked with decorative overlays — dots, flowers, stars, triangles and more — for dimensional poster and packaging work.
description: Dolcissimo is a hand-drawn geometric sans that doubles as a layered type system. The 28 styles break into functional weights (Thin, Regular, Rough, Outline, Script) and a wide range of decorative fill variants meant to be combined over the base letterforms for depth and texture. Its sweet spot is packaging, poster design and logo work where the stacking system earns its keep; outside those contexts, the family has limited reach.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describe Dolcissimo as a handwritten layered font family — a geometric sans given a hand-made warmth, paired with a full suite of decorative overlay styles for building expressive, multi-layer type compositions.

name: Two Fingers
classification_notes: Finger-drawn hand-lettered superfamily with six distinct sub-families: Skinny, Bodoni, Courier, Script, Poster and Icons. The Bodoni and Poster sub-families function as display faces; Script leans calligraphic; Courier provides a text-optimised mono-inflected variant. Rough and Super Rough texture variants run across most sub-families. No conventional weight axis – style differentiation is via sub-family and finish rather than stroke weight.
summary: A 20-style finger-drawn family by Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González, spanning Bodoni, Script, Courier, Poster and Skinny sub-families, each available in Regular, Rough and Super Rough variants.
description: Two Fingers was drawn mostly with the designers' actual index fingers – a creative exercise between Sofia and Turin that gives every style an energetic, irregular character no pen tool replicates. The six sub-families cover display, poster, calligraphic script, a text-sized Courier variant and a companion icon set, totalling 20 fonts. Best suited to editorial headlines, packaging and branding where deliberate hand-lettered imperfection is the intent.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describe Two Fingers as a handwritten family born between Sofia and Turin, with 90% of its glyphs drawn directly by finger. The complete family of 20 fonts covers a casual, fresh aesthetic alongside practical text variants, available with professional desktop and webfont licensing from the Resistenza shop.

name: Instamood
classification_notes: Casual, loosely hand-lettered sign-writing script with extensive OpenType ligatures. Offered in upright (Regular) and oblique (Slanted) variants only. Display-only character; not suited to body text or formal editorial work.
summary: A casual sign-writing script with abundant ligatures, built for social media graphics and informal display use.
description: Instamood is a two-style sign-writing script released in 2018 by Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González of Resistenza Type. Available in Regular and Slanted cuts, it relies on extensive ligatures to produce a loose, hand-lettered energy. The design targets social media graphics and casual display settings; it has no role in body text or formal editorial work.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describe Instamood as a new sign-writing script packed with ligatures, designed for Instagram posts and casual digital content.

name: Natura
classification_notes: Modern hand-calligraphy script drawn with a flexible fountain pen and digitised glyph by glyph. The family spans two script cuts (upright Regular and 16-degree Slanted) with extensive OpenType swashes and ligatures, a narrow grunge-textured serif subfamiy (Notebook), and two ornamental sets (Icons and Stamps). Predominantly a decorative script family with very limited text use.
summary: A fountain-pen calligraphy script inspired by nineteenth-century naturalist field notebooks, offered in upright and slanted script cuts alongside a narrow serif companion and two ornamental sets.
description: Natura was designed by drawing each letterform with a flexible fountain pen before digitising glyph by glyph, preserving the texture of dry ink on smooth paper. The core script cuts (Regular and Slanted) are rich in OpenType ligatures and swashes, making them suited to invitations, packaging and labels. The wider family adds Natura Notebook, a narrow grunge-edged serif, plus Icons and Stamps: hand-drawn ornaments and nature-themed decorative capitals.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describe Natura as rooted in a passion for modern hand-calligraphy, each character drafted first with a fountain pen to capture the feel of ink on paper. The inspiration came from the field notebooks of great natural world explorers, and the family extends that theme through hand-drawn botanical ornaments and stamp-style capitals alongside the core scripts.

name: Rachele
classification_notes: Monoline script inspired by Italian Bella Scrittura handwriting and Spencerian penmanship. No stroke contrast – the mono-weight line is its defining trait. Ships in three distinct subfamilies (standard, Noodle, Ribbon) across five widths from Ultra Condensed to Super Extended. Includes ligatures, swashes, alternates, small caps and ornaments. Cyrillic support puts it ahead of most scripts in language coverage.
summary: A monoline calligraphic script in the Spencerian tradition, released by Resistenza Type in three subfamilies and five widths, with Cyrillic support and extensive OpenType features.
description: Rachele is a monoline calligraphic script designed by Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González, drawing on Italian Bella Scrittura handwriting and Spencerian penmanship. The superfamily spans three subfamilies – standard, Noodle and Ribbon – each available across five widths (Ultra Condensed to Super Extended), with ligatures, swashes, alternates, small caps and ornaments throughout. Cyrillic coverage and 37-language Latin support give it broader reach than most scripts in its category. Use cases centre on wedding stationery, packaging, brand logos and greeting cards.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describes Rachele as a mono-line script inspired by the elegance of Italian handwriting tradition, blending historical calligraphic finesse with contemporary versatility – suited to feminine branding, chocolate packaging, invitations and editorial work that calls for flowing, connected letterforms.

name: Montana
classification_notes: Condensed-Grotesk skeleton overlaid with sketchy, handwritten strokes; monoline structure with low contrast; no confirmed italic or oblique variants in the published 7-font lineup; companion icons font ships with the family
summary: A condensed-Grotesk-inspired handwritten display family with four weights, a rough cut and a companion icons font, built for headlines, packaging and poster work.
description: Montana draws from tight, condensed Grotesk proportions and overlays handwritten, sketchy strokes to create a display face with a monoline, low-contrast structure. The family spans Light through Bold with a Rough variant and a separate Montana Icons font for illustrations and decorative elements. OpenType features include swashes, ligatures and alternates, broadening its expressive range at large sizes.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describe Montana as an elegantly playful handwritten font family that merges geometry and legibility with the originality of handwritten strokes. Designed for headlines, posters, t-shirts, food and wine packaging and digital applications, it is built around optimised legibility and a simple, low-contrast structure.

name: The Luxx
classification_notes: Display typeface rooted in the geometric letterforms of Italian art deco advertising and poster work from the 1930s. Seven stylistic variants layer distress, texture, open outline and multiline effects over the core design. Conceived entirely for headline and large-scale print use; not suitable for body text. No italics or condensed cuts.
summary: A seven-style art deco display family rooted in 1930s Italian advertising lettering, offered across clean, distressed, multiline and outline variants.
description: The Luxx takes its cue from the bold, geometric letterforms found on Italian art deco posters and advertising of the 1930s. First drawn in 2010 and redesigned in 2013, the family spans seven stylistic variants: Medium, Bold, Rough, Vintage, Multiline, Multiline Medium and Outline. It is built for large-scale use – poster headlines, luxury packaging, retro-inflected branding – and has little practical application at text sizes.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza Type is an independent digital type foundry run by Italian calligrapher Giuseppe Salerno and Spanish designer Paco González. The studio produces display, script and calligraphic typefaces, and offers professional desktop, web, app and digital advertising licences.

name: Copperlove
classification_notes: Single-style copperplate calligraphic script. Drawn with an oblique nib pen and sepia ink, it evokes the formal English copperplate tradition. OpenType alternates and swashes add decorative range but the family has no weight range, no condensed cuts, and no true italic — the script angle is intrinsic to the letterforms.
summary: A single-weight copperplate calligraphic script by Giuseppe Salerno, drawn with an oblique nib and sepia ink during a Berlin winter, with OpenType alternates and swashes.
description: Copperlove grew out of Giuseppe Salerno's copperplate calligraphy practice, drawn by hand with an oblique nib and sepia ink. The result is a fluid English-style script with genuine pen character rather than digitised stiffness. OpenType alternates and swashes give some expressive range, but with a single weight it is firmly a display and occasion face — invitations, logotypes, greeting cards.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describes Copperlove as having been born during a very long and hard winter in Berlin, created with an oblique nib and sepia ink as a homage to the English copperplate tradition, with many OpenType features including alternates and beautiful swashes.

name: Peperoncino
classification_notes: Decorative layered display sans-serif conceived with a marker pen. The 33-font family shares identical metrics to allow in-place stacking of texture and effect variants (Dots, Rough, Neon, Jeans, Doodle, 3D, etc.). Novelty/illustrative in intent rather than text-setting. Italian indie foundry by Giuseppe Salerno and Paco González.
summary: A 33-font layered display system drawn with a marker pen, designed for stacking its texture and effect variants on a shared baseline to build colourful, handmade headlines.
description: Peperoncino is a decorative display system conceived with a marker pen, its irregular strokes giving each cut a fresh handmade quality. The 33 fonts – spanning thin weights through texture variants like Dots, Rough, Neon, Jeans, Doodle, Blur and 3D – all share identical metrics, so a headline set in one style can be duplicated and layered in place to produce illustrative, multi-colour effects. Best suited to poster work, packaging and brand identities that call for a bold, hand-crafted typographic centrepiece.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describes Peperoncino as a decorative sans-serif designed first with a marker, with irregular strokes that create a fresh handmade feeling. The layered family includes several textures and shadows, and because each font shares the same metrics, a title set in one style can be copied and pasted in-place to build up layers of different weights and effects.

name: Merendina
classification_notes: Geometric letterform construction with an informal, hand-drawn touch; slanted variants rather than true italics; sometimes marketed as a kids/food display font; related to casual informal sans-serif traditions (cf. Futuramano, FF Providence Sans, North Bergen).
summary: A cheerful geometric display family with a hand-drawn quality, spanning six weights with matching slanted companions and OpenType swashes and alternates.
description: Merendina pairs a geometric skeleton with an informal, hand-drawn quality that gives it warmth without sacrificing structure. The 12-style family runs from Thin to Heavy, each weight accompanied by a slanted variant, and includes OpenType alternates and swashes for additional expressive range. It fits food branding, packaging, children's publishing and casual editorial work where a friendly, approachable tone is needed.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza Type describes Merendina as a geometric construction with a handwritten touch, available in six weights each with a slanted companion, totalling 12 fonts. The family includes OpenType alternates and swashes.

name: Adelaida
classification_notes: Handwritten display script with condensed, uppercase-weighted proportions and a light pencil-line quality. Three stylistic variants (Regular, Slanted, Multiline) rather than a conventional weight axis. No italics; Slanted is a design variant, not an oblique.
summary: Adelaida is a pencil-thin handwritten display script from Resistenza, spanning three stylistic variants suited to invitations, gift cards and short decorative copy.
description: Built around the look of pencil lettering, Adelaida is a light, condensed handwritten display font that keeps legibility in check within its decorative brief. The family covers three variants – Regular, Slanted and Multiline – giving some range without a conventional weight axis. It suits packaging, invitations and gift cards but is not meant for body text or extended reading.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza pitches Adelaida as thin like a pencil yet versatile and legible, recommending it for postcards, ads and gift cards.

name: Sonica Brush
classification_notes: All-caps handlettered brush script with a grungy, inky texture. Drawn with a Pentel brush on watercolour paper using sumi ink. Single weight, uppercase only, no lowercase. Carries the unpredictable stroke variation and rough edges of real brushwork rather than a digitally smoothed imitation.
summary: A single-weight all-caps brush script drawn with a Pentel brush and sumi ink, offering raw, grungy texture for poster headlines, apparel graphics and bold display work.
description: Sonica Brush is a grungy all-caps handlettered script produced by drawing directly with a Pentel brush on watercolour paper using sumi ink. The letterforms carry the unpredictable weight variation and ragged edges of real brushwork, giving it an authentically rough quality. It is a display-only face suited to posters, apparel, packaging and branding where an expressive, hand-drawn register is needed; its uppercase-only character limits everyday typesetting use.
foundry_blurb: Resistenza describe Sonica Brush as their first brush script, drawn by hand with a Pentel brush on watercolour paper. The result is an expressive uppercase face that captures the raw energy of ink on paper, with a grungy texture well suited to bold display applications.
